article_title: Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education
citation: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home
title: Khanmigo AI Component workflow architecture with declarative overrides
description: Each Khanmigo feature is a chat-based workflow with its own system prompt, guardrails, and configurable steps. The lowest-level building block is the AI Component: "a simple, generic function that we expect to have variable output, usually from an LLM call." Components are called through a single entry point providing standardized logging, offline-evaluation compatibility, and declarative dot-notation overrides of inputs such as prompt variables and model attributes. Because the workflow entry point is itself an AI Component, experiments can add, remove, or replace whole workflow steps.
requirements: A single entry point that automatically provides standardized logging and tracing, compatibility with offline evaluation tooling, and declarative input overrides
constraints: The platform is primarily written in Go with a small Python service supporting a Math Agent that runs student math in a sandbox with NumPy and SymPy
target_learners: K-12 students using Khanmigo Exercise and Tutor Me features
target_learning_goals: AI tutoring quality across math, science, essay writing, and humanities tutoring requests
examples: The Exercise chat workflow moderates student input, runs a Python Math Agent to identify math errors, and injects the Math Agent result as context before responding
key_sources: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home

article_title: Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education
citation: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home
title: Offline evaluation datasets and calibrated LLM judges for tutoring behaviors
description: The team maintains targeted offline datasets sampled from production completions, including an answer-giveaway dataset where "The final dataset consists of 63 data points" and a Tutor Me input-classification dataset where "the dataset consisted of 794 data points." LLM judges calibrated against human experts measure cognitive engagement, math errors, and answer giveaway; the engagement judge shows "an F1 score of 0.83, Matthews Correlation Coefficient of 0.75, false positive rate of 0.08, and false negative rate of 0.17."
requirements: Datasets must be stripped of PII and kept up to date as user behavior drifts; judge prompts are published as supplemental material
constraints: Offline evaluations currently evaluate only a single turn of a model; user simulation has been explored only in limited contexts
target_learning_goals: Measuring answer giveaway, request classification, math accuracy, and cognitive engagement in tutoring conversations
examples: The giveaway dataset was built by sampling production completions, running an LLM judge, filtering to giveaway cases, and filtering to cases where a human expert agreed with the judge label
key_sources: Udeshi, T., Khazenzon, A., Khan, K., Breen, N., Corwin, R., DiGiano, C., Weatherholtz, K., Zaluski, M. (2026). Methodologies for Improving the Quality of AI Tutoring in K-12 Education. https://sites.google.com/khanacademy.org/aied2026supplementalmaterial/home

article_title: Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention
citation: Daniel P. Kelly and Teomara Rutherford. (2017). Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention. International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning, 18(4). https://www.irrodl.org
title: Khan Academy as a computer-based supplemental mathematics intervention
description: Khan Academy is a large, free open educational resource offering video-based lectures paired with problems for students to solve, with points and badges that "serve to provide positive reinforcement and encouragement." In this study it was used by seventh graders for a minimum of 30 minutes per class over four weeks as a self-paced, self-directed supplement, with students free to choose topics, simulating typical at-home use. The platform internally tracks metrics including minutes spent, points attained, and topics mastered.
requirements: Requires student access to the platform and time allocated within or alongside class; in this study time was tracked by the classroom teacher and used as a daily participation grade
constraints: The study examined only use as it might occur at home without a teacher's guidance or knowledge; students were not assigned specific topics
target_learning_goals: mathematics achievement on standardized end-of-grade assessment content
examples: Treatment students worked with Khan Academy a minimum of 30 minutes per class over a four-week period without assigned topics
key_sources: Daniel P. Kelly and Teomara Rutherford. (2017). Khan Academy as Supplemental Instruction: A Controlled Study of a Computer-Based Mathematics Intervention. International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning, 18(4). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1146230
